notes: The Octopus Card works everywhere (MTR, tram, ferry, shops). Buy it at the airport. The Airport Express takes 24 minutes.
October to December is the best season (22°C, dry). In January and February it's 15°C, a cardigan is enough and it's ideal for walking.
Dim sum is eaten in the morning and at lunchtime. Queues are normal at cheap Michelin spots like Tim Ho Wan and Kam's Roast Goose.
Tipping is not expected, and a 10% service charge is added to the bill. Cash is still common, and small restaurants don't take cards.
The Star Ferry and Peak Tram are Hong Kong rituals. Go up to the Peak at 08:00, and return at 19:00 for the evening lights.
You need your passport for Macau. Ferries to Lamma and Cheung Chau leave from Central Piers 4 and 5.

transit.name: Octopus Card
transit.why_chosen: It works on the MTR, trams, buses, the Star Ferry and in shops, so it covers everything in Hong Kong.

stops.name: Peak Tram
stops.tips: The first trams at 07:30 have no queue. It's an 8-minute ride to Victoria Peak, around 88 HKD return.

stops.name: Victoria Peak Sky Terrace 428
stops.tips: Terrace at the summit with 360° views of the harbour. The morning haze burns off.

stops.name: Peak Circle Walk
stops.tips: A flat, shaded 3.5 km walk around the summit with great views.

stops.name: Tim Ho Wan Central
stops.tips: The cheapest Michelin-starred dim sum in the world. Don't miss the BBQ pork buns (char siu bao).

stops.name: Central Mid-Levels Escalator
stops.tips: The world's longest outdoor covered escalator system. It takes you up to SoHo and Tai Kwun.

backups.name: Lan Fong Yuen
backups.tips: A cha chaan teng (Hong Kong-style café) open since 1952. Try the milk tea and the pork chop sandwich.

backups.name: Tai Kwun
backups.tips: A former police station and prison, now a free cultural centre.

stops.name: Star Ferry Central Pier
stops.tips: The legendary 8-minute ferry from Central to Tsim Sha Tsui. 5 HKD with an Octopus card.

stops.name: Tsim Sha Tsui Promenade
stops.tips: The Avenue of Stars and harbour views. Good for morning photos.

stops.name: Hong Kong Museum of Art
stops.tips: An art museum on the waterfront. Free entry, with Chinese calligraphy and contemporary art.

stops.name: Mak's Noodle Jordan
stops.tips: The classic wonton noodles. The bowls are small, so order 2.

stops.name: Temple Street Night Market
stops.tips: Fortune tellers, street food and cheap goods. It comes alive after 18:00, so try the claypot rice.

backups.name: Australia Dairy Company
backups.tips: Scrambled egg toast and steamed milk pudding. The queue moves fast.

backups.name: Kowloon Park
backups.tips: A park in Tsim Sha Tsui with flamingos. An alternative to the museum.

stops.name: Ngong Ping 360 Cable Car
stops.tips: A 25-minute cable car ride from Tung Chung (around 300 HKD return, glass-bottom cabin extra). You get views of the sea and mountains.

stops.name: Tian Tan Buddha
stops.tips: A 34 m bronze Buddha. Climb the 268 steps for views over Lantau.

stops.name: Po Lin Monastery
stops.tips: The monastery at the foot of the Buddha. Vegetarian meal tickets are sold here.

stops.name: Po Lin Vegetarian Restaurant
stops.tips: The monastery's vegetarian kitchen. Simple and tasty.

stops.name: Tai O Fishing Village
stops.tips: A village of stilt houses. A boat trip (with a chance of spotting pink dolphins) costs 30 HKD, and there's a dried fish market.

backups.name: Tai O Dried Seafood Market
backups.tips: Grilled seafood in Tai O. An alternative to the monastery meal.

backups.name: Wisdom Path
backups.tips: A path of wooden sutra pillars next to the Buddha. A short walk.

days.theme: Mong Kok and Sham Shui Po

stops.name: Chi Lin Nunnery
stops.tips: A Tang-style wooden nunnery built without nails, with lotus ponds.

stops.name: Nan Lian Garden
stops.tips: A Chinese garden opposite the nunnery, with a golden pagoda.

stops.name: Wong Tai Sin Temple
stops.tips: Fortune sticks (kau cim) and incense. The busiest temple in Hong Kong.

stops.name: Kwan Kee Bamboo Noodle
stops.tips: In Sham Shui Po, noodles kneaded with a bamboo pole. Legendary flavour.

stops.name: Sham Shui Po Apliu Street
stops.tips: An electronics and fabric market in Hong Kong's most local neighbourhood, with street food.

backups.name: Tim Ho Wan Sham Shui Po
backups.tips: The first Tim Ho Wan branch.

stops.name: Dragon's Back Trail
stops.tips: Hong Kong's most famous ridge hike (2 hours, easy to moderate). It has views of Shek O and is ideal in winter.

stops.name: Stanley Market
stops.tips: A market in a seaside town. Good for silk and souvenirs.

stops.name: The Boathouse Stanley
stops.tips: Seafood on the Stanley waterfront, with a terrace.

stops.name: Stanley Promenade
stops.tips: Murray House and the seafront. Stop for a coffee.

stops.name: Shek O Village
stops.tips: The village where the ridge hike ends. There's a beach and a Thai restaurant.

backups.name: Deep Water Bay
backups.tips: A quieter bay next to Repulse Bay.

stops.name: Yung Shue Wan Lamma
stops.tips: Take the Macau ferry (1 hour, around 180 HKD) to see the Ruins of St. Paul's and Senado Square. You need your passport.

stops.name: Lamma Family Trail
stops.tips: A walk taking in A-Ma Temple and Taipa Village.

stops.name: Ruins of St. Paul's
stops.tips: The church facade that symbolises Macau. Portuguese heritage.

stops.name: Lord Stow's Bakery Macau
stops.tips: Portuguese-style pastel de nata (custard tart). A Macau classic.

stops.name: Senado Square
stops.tips: A mosaic-paved square with Portuguese buildings. The return ferry to Hong Kong leaves at 18:00.

backups.name: Macau Tower
backups.tips: A tower with bungee jumping and views over Macau.

stops.name: Hong Kong Park
stops.tips: A park among the skyscrapers, with an aviary and a lake.

stops.name: Ding Ding Tram Line
stops.tips: Ride the historic double-decker tram to Wan Chai. Take a front seat on the upper deck, 3 HKD.

stops.name: Kam's Roast Goose Wan Chai
stops.tips: Michelin-starred goose. A farewell lunch, with a 30-minute queue.

stops.name: Airport Express Hong Kong Station
stops.tips: The airport train takes 24 minutes. You can check in in the city.

backups.name: Joy Hing Roasted Meat
backups.tips: Cheap char siu in Wan Chai.

backups.name: Blue House Wan Chai
backups.tips: A blue historic building and neighbourhood museum. An alternative to the tram.
